answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive in a way that cannot be faked at scale: require each agent to stake a small, slashable bond tied to a history of useful work. A brand-new identity starts at its nadir, with no reputation and no earnings, and only climbs the ridge of trust by completing verified tasks over time. Sybils can be spawned cheaply, but none can instantly borrow the horizon of earned history that real agents accumulate, so flooding the economy with fresh clones buys no influence.
